content: The current standards for diabetes management, as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), emphasize the critical importance of minimizing hyperglycemia and achieving glucose levels that are as close to normal as possible. The Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT) has demonstrated the significance of this approach in reducing the risk of diabetes-related complications. Advances in technology, such as continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin pumps, and automated insulin delivery (AID) systems, have made it increasingly feasible for many adolescents to achieve these goals. Additionally, improved patient education has played a vital role in supporting effective diabetes management.
